title: Problem and product intent
body: Theme frequency and sentiment do not explain how respondents mentioning a topic score on a business outcome. Analysts need the topic’s own KPI and its observed relationship to the overall KPI.

Impact on KPI presents one compact table: themes and expandable sub-themes, observed impact, a named KPI, unique response count and share of the eligible base. Include one default Impact on KPI widget in every TextAI dashboard.

Primary users are CX/EX analysts prioritizing investigation and reviewers validating results against responses. Select a widget type first, then its text question, then configure the KPI. The table supports comparison, not predicted lift.
Review draft updated 4 October 2026. TextAI tables and settings provide the visual baseline; BI custom metrics inform the scoring setup.

title: Scope of these requirements
body: Widget-first creation across TextAI: widget type → text question/variable → KPI setup for Impact on KPI.
Inherited dashboard source, searchable question table, pagination and immediate question-to-KPI navigation.
Named KPI, same-source outcome field, metric type, answer mapping and decimal precision.
Configurable NPS, CSAT, CES and mean; paired response bases and observed impact.
Single-table presentation, header tooltips, sorting, expansion, settings, filters and response evidence.
Default widget on every dashboard; acceptance checks and product boundaries.

title: Data contract
subtitle: Inherited source + text field + configured KPI field
body: Inherit the dashboard’s survey/dataset; do not ask users to select the source again. Bind stable source, text-field and KPI-field IDs. Join analyzed text and tags to the KPI answer by response ID within that source, never row order or sentiment.

B is the unique response base after filters, with completed analysis, nonblank text and an included, valid KPI answer. Missing/invalid answers, blank/pending/failed text and answer options mapped to Exclude do not enter B.

T is the subset of B mentioning a theme/sub-theme; R = B excluding T. Parent membership is a deduplicated union of response IDs, not the sum of child counts. Sub-themes use B, not a parent-only denominator.

One widget binds one text field to one named KPI configuration. Use separate widgets for different outcome questions or formulas; each has an independent eligible base. Never pool different KPIs into one impact.

Store question ID, metric type, answer mappings, CES calculation and precision with the widget configuration. Discover eligible fields from the selected source and join text and KPI answers by response ID.

title: Calculation rules
subtitle: Use saved answer mappings; round only for display
body: NPS(S) = 100 × (promoter count − detractor count) / included count in S. Passives remain in the denominator. Standard 0–10 defaults are 9–10 promoter, 7–8 passive, 0–6 detractor; user mappings determine the calculation.
CSAT(S) = 100 × satisfied count / included count. Mean(S) = sum of configured answer scores / included count. Excluded options leave both numerator and denominator; a score of zero is valid.

CES calculation must be explicit: Average score (default) = sum of configured effort scores / count; Percentage easy = 100 × easy / count; Net easy = 100 × (easy − difficult) / count. Neutral responses remain in percentage bases.
Overall = KPI(B); topic KPI = KPI(T); Impact = KPI(B) − KPI(R). Equivalently, |T|/|B| × [KPI(T) − KPI(R)]. Responses = |T|; Share of base = 100 × |T|/|B|.

Precision is configurable from 0–5 decimal places for KPI and impact; shares use 1. Percent-based scores use % and impact pp; NPS/net CES/means use pts. Keep full calculation precision. Overlapping topic impacts are not additive or causal.

title: Worked example
subtitle: Theme score and impact answer different questions
body: Eligible base B: 1,000 responses, 600 promoters, 200 passives and 200 detractors. Overall NPS = 100 × (600 − 200) / 1,000 = +40.
Theme T: 200 responses, 60 promoters, 40 passives and 100 detractors. Theme NPS = 100 × (60 − 100) / 200 = −20. Share of base = 200 / 1,000 = 20%.
Remaining group R: 800 responses, 540 promoters, 160 passives and 100 detractors. NPS excluding the theme = 100 × (540 − 100) / 800 = +55.
Observed impact = +40 − (+55) = −15 NPS points. Cross-check: 20% × (−20 − 55) = −15.

Read the row as: respondents mentioning this theme have NPS −20; including them lowers this eligible base’s NPS by 15 points versus the remaining group. This is an observed difference, not a causal estimate or a promise of improvement.

title: Table and interactions
subtitle: One widget header and one hierarchical table
body: Title: Impact on KPI. Columns: Theme / subtheme, Impact (pts or pp), user-defined KPI name, Responses, Share of base. Keep headers on one line; truncate long KPI names with full text available on hover.

Put a separate info icon to the LEFT of Impact, named KPI and Share of base. Tooltips explain the active formula/base and exclusions; impact is an observed difference, not predicted lift. Hover and keyboard focus work without sorting.

Show signed impact with diverging bars sharing one symmetric scale across parents and children. Column clicks toggle sorting; default is signed impact ascending. Keep children under parents and unavailable values last.

Use response-viewer sort icons and shared expand/collapse icons, including an icon-only expand-all control. Start collapsed. Show themes limits parent rows after sorting, without changing scores or calculation bases.

Keep Overall at the bottom outside sorting: baseline KPI, eligible count, 100% share and impact —. Use flush header/footer edges and content-sized height. No subtitle, sample badge, eye icon, separate summaries or blank footer padding.

title: Create a widget
subtitle: Widget type FIRST, then question, then KPI setup
body: All TextAI Add widget flows begin with widget-type selection, BEFORE question selection. Choose Impact on KPI → Next → the dashboard’s analyzed text questions/variables. Other widget types retain their own completion steps.

The Data source step inherits the dashboard source. Show ONLY search, the questions/variables table and pagination (10 rows per page). No data-source label or dropdown. Search filters the table and resets pagination.

Clicking a question/variable immediately opens the flat KPI setup step; there is no Next action on the question step. Back/breadcrumb navigation retains valid draft choices and search; Cancel clears the draft.

KPI setup is left-aligned. Order: required KPI name → required same-source KPI question/variable → metric type → metric-specific answer configuration → decimal precision. This is not a segment builder: no filter operators or condition-value selectors.

Disable Metric type until a KPI field is selected. Require a nonblank name, selected field, valid mapping of every available option and at least one included option before Add widget. Adding binds the complete configuration to this widget.
For another outcome, add another widget or edit Analytics. Do not infer an undefined numeric field’s metric from its name. With no compatible KPI fields, explain the empty state and prevent creation.

title: Widget settings
subtitle: Shared settings surface; full KPI editing in Analytics
body: General contains only shared Show name / Widget name and Filter options. Widget name is distinct from the KPI name shown in the score column. Keep KPI question and scoring configuration out of General.

Analytics reuses the full setup editor: KPI name, question/variable, metric type (NPS, CSAT, CES, Mean), answer mappings, CES calculation and precision. NPS maps promoter/passive/detractor; CSAT maps satisfied/not satisfied; CES uses scores or easy/neutral/difficult; all support Exclude.

Mean and average CES allow a numeric score for each option. Changing field or metric rebuilds compatible defaults for review. Valid edits recalculate preview, base, column label, units and impacts; invalid drafts show an error without calculating partial mappings.

Use the standard WickUI precision dropdown: 0 (1), 1 (0.1), 2 (0.01), 3 (0.001), 4 (0.0001), 5 (0.00001). Retain Show themes and Show Overall baseline. Design uses shared colors/typography; no default-expansion toggle.

Filters: Dashboard, Widget, Combined (intersection), None. Apply filters before every calculation; production access rules always apply. No save/session/reset notices, Reset settings button or redundant question/matching prose. Formula guidance belongs with mapping controls and header tooltips.

title: Inspect the supporting evidence
body: Click a theme/sub-theme, impact bar or response count to inspect its eligible responses. Show KPI name and metric, group score, overall score, score excluding the group, observed impact and comparison count.
Each response shows its text, topic context and actual selected KPI answer. Use the saved scoring mappings for calculations. Sentiment may provide context but never determines the KPI.

Searching inside the response dialog filters only that list; it must not change the widget’s base or impact. Closing returns to the current table state. Changing KPI configuration/response filters must not leave stale drilldown results.

Overall opens analysis details: text field, KPI field, configured formula, eligible count, excluded count and text coverage. Coverage = 100 × eligible paired responses / included valid KPI responses after the same filters.
The Overall baseline is the paired text-and-KPI population and can differ from the all-survey KPI. Keep coverage and methodology in details, not separate permanent widget sections.

title: Empty, small and changing groups
subtitle: Unavailable is different from zero
body: No eligible responses: show an empty state, unavailable KPI/impact, Overall count 0 and share —. Missing/deleted/inaccessible fields require re-selection; never silently substitute another field.
No matching topic responses or no remaining comparison group: impact is — with the reason. A genuine zero difference stays zero at the configured precision; never display unavailable as zero.
Small sample flags a nonempty topic group or comparison group below 30 responses. This is a caution threshold, not a significance test. Parent/child counts must reconcile by unique response ID.

Reject blank KPI names, missing fields, unmapped/nonfinite scores and all-excluded mappings. Metric type stays disabled until field selection. Clearing an invalid draft must not corrupt the last valid calculation.

Response filters recompute B, T and R together. Sorting, expansion, pagination and display limits change presentation only. Production loading/errors must not present old scores as the newly selected KPI.

title: Scope and production boundary
body: In scope: widget-first creation, one named text-to-KPI binding per widget, configurable NPS/CSAT/CES/mean, answer exclusions and precision, hierarchical table, tooltips, shared settings, filtering and response drilldown.
Include one default Impact on KPI widget on every TextAI dashboard.
Question selection inherits the dashboard’s source. Discover compatible survey questions or dataset variables and use their response-level answers.

Requirements include source/field discovery, response-ID joins, filter/access semantics and refresh/error handling. Confirm configuration persistence, CES/report formula parity, supported scales, lower-is-better direction, weighting and dashboard theme-filter behavior.
Out of scope: regression Driver Score, causal attribution, predicted KPI lift, additive decomposition across overlapping themes, arbitrary cross-source joins and scoring undefined fields by label.

title: Acceptance criteria
subtitle: Functional and visual release checks
body: AC-01 Creation: widget selection comes first; the question step has only search/table/pagination, no source selector. Clicking a question opens KPI setup immediately. Back retains the draft; Cancel resets it.

AC-02 Setup: left-aligned name/field/metric/configuration controls; Metric disabled until KPI selection. Add requires complete valid mappings. Survey uses question labels and dataset uses variable labels; separate widgets remain independent.

AC-03 Calculation: reproduce 40 overall, −20 topic, 55 excluding, −15 impact, 200 responses and 20% share. Verify remapped NPS, CSAT, CES variants, custom mean, exclusions, duplicate IDs and true zero/unavailable cases.

AC-04 Presentation: the KPI name is the score header; info icons sit left of Impact/KPI/Share headers. Tooltips match active formulas, work by keyboard and do not sort. Shared icons, single-line headers, flush edges and content-sized height are retained.

AC-05 Settings: Analytics edits all KPI fields/mappings and 0–5 precision; invalid drafts never calculate. Filter modes recompute the full base. Sorting keeps hierarchy and Overall last. Drilldown counts/answers reconcile; dialog search does not change the KPI.
AC-06 Lifecycle: each dashboard has a default KPI widget. Verify small-sample and empty states, response integration and the agreed configuration lifecycle.

title: Prototype walkthrough
subtitle: Walk through the final widget-first experience
body: Open https://survey-re.vercel.app/ → TextAI → dashboard (/text-ai/1). Confirm the default Impact on KPI widget.
Add widget → select Impact on KPI FIRST → Next → search the question table → click a question to enter KPI setup immediately. Confirm no source dropdown or extra Next action. Check Back and Cancel.

Enter KPI name, choose KPI question, then metric and answer mappings. Verify Metric is disabled before question selection. Change precision through the standard 0–5 dropdown and add the widget; confirm the named score header and dynamic units.

In Analytics, edit the question/formula/mappings, including CES calculation and excluded options. Compare two widgets for different KPIs. Test column sorting, expansion, left-side tooltips, filters, drilldown and Overall details.
Review the creation flow, metric settings, header tooltips, sorting, expansion, filters and supporting responses against the acceptance criteria.
